subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Docker host IPC for agent sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow typed break-glass field rather than generic raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: The remaining request changes the sandbox isolation boundary and public config contract; source inspection shows the safe typed GPU subset is already implemented but host IPC/raw args remain absent.

options.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
options.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, security-audit coverage, Docker create-args support, and tests while keeping generic raw args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Keep GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and leave host IPC unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define namespace policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
recommendation.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, security-audit coverage, Docker create-args support, and tests while keeping generic raw args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is closest to the sandbox namespace/security-boundary policy history represented by the container namespace join hardening work.
